correctness.rationale: The strict one-site comparison gives d>|h_i| for a vacancy, and sigma h_i>d for a sign sigma, where h_i is the sum of the two neighboring spins. Thus at d=0 only the uniform signs survive. At 0<d<1 a mixed state consists exactly of isolated vacancies separating alternating sign-runs of length at least two: a zero needs opposite or both zero neighbors, a sign cannot neighbor its opposite, and a sign at a vacancy needs a same-sign neighbor on its other side. A vacancy block of length at least two cannot border a sign. The alternating runs require even k; the k run lengths sum to n-k with all lengths at least two. Counting a marked labeled vacancy and first sign, then removing the k choices of mark, yields (2n/k) binomial(n-2k-1,k-1), in addition to the three uniform states. At d=1 a single matching neighbor with a vacancy opposite is no longer sufficient; at d=2 even two matching neighbors are no longer sufficient. This confirms both transition equalities under the neutral-move convention. With f=zx^3/(1-x), the even-run-length sum is 2x f f_x/(1-f^2). For fixed positive z near 1, f(r,z)=1 gives a unique simple dominant pole: equality of absolute values on |x|=r would require x^3 and x^4 and every subsequent power to have the same phase, forcing x=r. The pole has principal part x/(r-x); the uniform states are exponentially negligible there. The equation for lambda(z)=1/r yields the entropy and the derivative in log z gives 1/(lambda^2+3). Exponential Markov bounds with small fixed positive/negative log z prove concentration from the limiting log moment generating function, without requiring differentiation of a pointwise limit. value.rationale: Vacancies create isolated strictly absorbing interfaces although opposite signs cannot form a direct stable interface. The proof identifies the only field window with nonuniform traps and explains the fate of all configurations at neutral-move boundaries. The exact labeled polynomial supplies more than the entropy: it counts the traps at every vacancy number and yields a concrete macroscopic vacancy density under uniform sampling of the traps, without implying dynamical sampling probabilities.
